Students must not use generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools or AI-powered websites in ways which breach assessment instructions, for example to generate content, answers, or references.
The use of ghost writing services (whether paid or not) is strictly prohibited in all assessed work and, if identified, will be considered an extremely serious breach of the University’s regulations.
Plagiarism is defined as the submission or presentation of work, in any form, which is not one's own, without proper acknowledgement of the source(s).
Working jointly to prepare an assignment or examination answers is considered collusion.
Students must not re-use work they have submitted for assessment either at this University or any other institution, because this would result in credit being awarded twice for the same effort.

process.quote: The Head of School will refer all Honours and postgraduate level cases, and all repeat allegations, directly to the Student Conduct Team for investigation under the Code of Student Conduct.
The Head of School will refer all Honours and postgraduate level cases, and all repeat allegations, directly to the Student Conduct Team for investigation under the Code of Student Conduct.
At the interview, the student will be given a clear explanation of what is alleged and will be given the opportunity to respond, and to admit or deny responsibility.
With respect to undergraduate non-Honours cases that are first breaches, the Head of School will interview the student concerned.

The student has the right to be accompanied, assisted or represented at the interview by one of the following: a parent or guardian; another student or friend; an Adviser from the Students’ Representative Council Advice Centre; a member of University staff, or any other person.
The student has the right of appeal to the Senate Assessors for Student Conduct in respect of any penalty imposed by the Head of School.
A student who wishes to appeal must do so in writing to student-conduct@glasgow.ac.uk within 10 working days of the date of the Head of School’s written decision.
If the Head of School is satisfied, on the balance of probabilities, that a breach has occurred they may impose an academic penalty, which will take account of the extent of the misconduct.
